name: Hard Mode
description: Raises enemy durability and offence for a real difficulty spike, then pays it back with a large experience and coin boost. The balance target is a shorter, denser loop rather than a longer grind: fights are meaningfully more dangerous, but you level faster and clear them in less total time.
notes: This profile stores only multipliers. It contains no bytes, names, stats or other data derived from the retail ROM.
Stats are applied to the user's own data export at build time.
Values are stored as unsigned 16-bit fields, so every result is clamped to 65535.

Balance is derived from the reconstructed damage formula in PiT src/battle/battle_damage_calculation.c: damage = (attacker_level * attacker_power) / defender_defense. Defense is a divisor, not a subtrahend.

Turns to kill therefore scale with max_hp * defense multiplied together, not added. The previous HP x1.5 + DEF x1.5 draft produced x2.25 turns per battle with no experience compensation, which is what made it read as a slog.
These values give about x1.15 turns per battle, x2.3 damage taken per battle, and x0.66 total turns spent per level gained.

transforms.reason: Enemy HP +10%. Deliberately small: HP is a direct turns-to-kill multiplier, and this is the stat that turns a difficulty spike into a slog.
Enemy POW +100%. This is the difficulty spike. It raises damage taken per turn directly, so it makes fights feel dangerous without making them longer.
Enemy DEF +5%. Kept near 1x on purpose: defense is the divisor in the damage formula, so it multiplies with HP into the turn count and can floor small hits to 1.
Enemy SPD +25%. Drives turn order and hit-bonus pressure without multiplying damage or length.
Coin rewards +75%, so the extra danger pays for itself in shop budget.
Experience +75%. Experience is a flat per-enemy award with no dependence on HP or turns, so this is the lever that actually shortens the progression loop.
